title: Watch: BBC witnesses 'taxi boat' picking up migrants multiple times in a day
summary:
A BBC investigation has found smuggling gangs are running low on small boats, forcing rival gangs to have to work together to meet demand for crossings.
With crossings at a six-year low, it includes loading more migrants on larger vessels, as the 'mega-dinghies' that were first seen last month.
The gangs claim more are being prepared.

title: Spain's leader struggles to answer lawmakers about Ceuta border crisis
summary:
While rejecting suggestions that Moroccan authorities helped orchestrate the incident, Sánchez said Moroccan police "allowed the border to be crossed."
Last week, Spain's Defense Minister Margarita Robles said Spanish intelligence had provided prior warning of the border rush, while Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said it had not.
Sánchez faced a barrage of questions on Thursday from lawmakers after his opening address alongside calls for early elections.
Questions about Morocco's roleSánchez also maintained there was no evidence Morocco's government was behind the mass crossing.
Sánchez condemned comments from two Moroccan ministers questioning the sovereignty of Ceuta and Melilla, Spain's other territory in North Africa.

title: ICE officer faces federal charges for lying over shooting of Venezuelan immigrant
summary:
ICE officer faces federal charges for lying over shooting of Venezuelan immigranttoggle caption Michael Gonzalez/AP PhotoFederal prosecutors have brought charges against an officer with Immigration and Customs Enforcement for lying to investigators about a shooting of a Venezuelan man in Minnesota earlier this year.
The charges represent a rare moment of the Justice Department seeking to hold immigration officers accountable for their actions and tactics while conducting arrests.
Christian Castro, the ICE officer, was in north Minneapolis in January as part of a broad immigration crackdown in the state known as Operation Metro Surge.
Sosa-Celis's attorney criticized the new federal charges against Castro, saying the ICE officer "lied to cover up the fact that he shot my client through the door of an occupied house without a self-defense justification."
Sponsor MessageFederal immigration officers have shot at more than 20 people under the Trump administration's immigration crackdown.

title: New immigration court tactic leads to huge lines and chaos in Miami
summary:
New immigration court tactic leads to huge lines and chaos in Miamitoggle caption Eva Marie Uzcategui for NPRMIAMI — Yerandy Gonzalez looks at the line of hundreds of people in front of him and shakes his head.
The line — which stretches across a few blocks on this humid Tuesday morning — is of people waiting to go inside Miami's immigration court.
"It's a very unfair, but a very effective tactic," said David Wilson, the vice chair of the American Immigration Lawyers Association's immigration court committee.
In the Miami immigration court, the increase of in-absentia orders in July spiked from 1,383 in May to 2,886 in July — a 108% increase.
toggle caption Eva Marie Uzcategui for NPRStanding in line outside the Miami immigration court, she says she's concerned about everything.

title: ICE agent charged with lying about shooting Venezuelan man during crackdown
summary:
A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent has been charged with lying about the non-fatal shooting of a Venezuelan migrant in the state of Minnesota.
Christian Castro, who is not yet in custody, faces a six-count federal indictment relating to shooting on 14 January, according to the BBC's US media partner CBS.
The Department of Homeland Security initially said he fired in self-defence after being attacked by three Venezuelan illegal migrants with a shovel and broom handle.
Minnesota investigators allege Castro fired through a closed door, shooting the man in the leg.
It is rare for the current justice department to accuse a federal agent of breaking the law on the job.

title: Burnham, Macron talk border security and stronger Europe-UK ties
summary:
New UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham discussed shared challenges in his first official meeting with the French president.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and French President Emmanuel Macron have held talks about migration, the war in Ukraine and trade during an official meeting in London.
“The progress we have seen this summer shows what can be achieved when the UK and France work together,” Burnham said.
The British prime minister is also seeking closer post-Brexit cooperation with Europe in a bid to boost sluggish domestic growth.
“The Prime Minister set out how the Made in Europe agenda could pose significant challenges for UK industry,” a UK government spokesperson said.

title: Spain’s PM says no evidence Morocco planned Ceuta border rush
summary:
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez says Madrid has found no evidence that Morocco orchestrated a surge of 70,000 people who crossed into its North African enclave of Ceuta a month ago.
Speaking in parliament on Thursday, Sanchez responded to claims in a police report that emerged this week and suggested the border rush into Ceuta in late July was planned to overwhelm border controls.
“I can assure you that no institution – not the diplomatic service nor the European Commission nor any international body – has provided the Spanish government with any solid evidence that Morocco planned or carried out the incident.
In late July, about 72,000 people swam and rushed into Ceuta, a Spanish enclave with a population of 84,000 that borders Morocco.
Sanchez has defended Morocco during the crisis, highlighting Rabat’s cooperation in returning most of the migrants within 48 hours.
